title: Water

notes.heading: 1. Temporary vs Permanent Hardness & CaCO₃ Equivalents (ppm)
notes.proseLatex: Hard water fails to lather with soap because $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ precipitate insoluble calcium/magnesium stearates ($2\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{35}\text{COONa} + \text{Ca}^{2+} \to (\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{35}\text{COO})_2\text{Ca}\downarrow$). TEMPORARY (carbonate) hardness comes from dissolved $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$ and $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$, whereas PERMANENT (non-carbonate) hardness comes from $\text{CaCl}_2, \text{MgCl}_2, \text{CaSO}_4, \text{MgSO}_4$. Hardness is universally expressed in ppm ($\text{mg/L}$) of $\text{CaCO}_3$ equivalent because molar mass of $\text{CaCO}_3$ is a convenient $100\text{ g/mol}$ (equivalent weight $= 50$).

keyFormulas.label: CaCO₃ Equivalent Conversion & Hardness Units
keyFormulas.latex: $\text{Eq. of CaCO}_3 = W_{\text{salt}} \times \frac{100}{M_{\text{divalent salt}}},\qquad 1\text{ ppm} = 1\text{ mg/L} = 0.1^\circ\text{Fr} = 0.07^\circ\text{Cl}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Convert mg/L of CaSO4(136), MgSO4(120), CaCl2(111), MgCl2(95), Ca(HCO3)2(162) into ppm CaCO3.

examples.problemLatex: A water sample contains $13.6\text{ mg/L}$ of $\text{CaSO}_4$ ($M=136$) and $9.5\text{ mg/L}$ of $\text{MgCl}_2$ ($M=95$). Find its total hardness in ppm $\text{CaCO}_3$.
stepsLatex: $\text{MgCl}_2$ contribution $= 9.5 \times \frac{100}{95} = 10\text{ mg/L} = 10\text{ ppm}$, giving total hardness $= 20\text{ ppm}$.

notes.heading: 2. Boiling, Clark's Lime, Permutit (Zeolite), Calgon & Ion-Exchange Resins
notes.proseLatex: BOILING or Clark's calculated-lime method ($\text{Ca(OH)}_2$) removes ONLY temporary hardness ($\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaCO}_3\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$, while $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$ precipitates as $\text{Mg(OH)}_2\downarrow$!). Permanent + temporary hardness are removed by: (a) Permutit/Zeolite ($\text{Na}_2\text{Ze}$, hydrated sodium aluminosilicate, regenerated by $10\%\text{ NaCl}$ brine), (b) Calgon ($\text{Na}_6\text{P}_6\text{O}_{18}$, sequesters $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ into soluble $[\text{Na}_2\text{CaP}_6\text{O}_{18}]^{2-}$), and (c) Ion-exchange resins ($\text{R-H}^+$ + $\text{R'-OH}^-$, yielding demineralized/deionized water removing ALL cations and anions!).

keyFormulas.label: Zeolite Softening, Regeneration & Calgon Complexation
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compare boiling, zeolite (leaves Na+ salts), Calgon, and mixed-bed deionization.

notes.heading: 3. EDTA Complexometric Titration, Potable Disinfection & BOD/COD
notes.proseLatex: Hardness is assayed quantitatively by complexometric titration with disodium EDTA at $\text{pH} \approx 10$ ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ buffer) using Eriochrome Black-T (EBT) indicator: wine-red $[\text{Mg-EBT}]$ turns pure blue at the endpoint as EDTA forms stabler $1:1$ chelates with $\text{Ca}^{2+}/\text{Mg}^{2+}$. Municipal disinfection uses chlorination ($\text{HOCl}$ active germicide), bleaching powder ($\text{CaOCl}_2$), or ozonation; organic pollution is tracked via Biochemical Oxygen Demand ($\text{BOD}_5$ at $20^\circ\text{C}$) and Chemical Oxygen Demand ($\text{COD}$, acidic $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, always $\text{COD} \ge \text{BOD}$!).

keyFormulas.label: EDTA Titration Conditions & COD ≥ BOD
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Recall EBT colour change, pH 10 buffer, and why COD exceeds BOD.

wbjeebTraps: Boiling $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$ precipitates $\text{Mg(OH)}_2\downarrow$ (because $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ has lower $K_{sp}$ than $\text{MgCO}_3$), whereas $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$ precipitates $\text{CaCO}_3\downarrow$!
Zeolite process removes hardness ($\text{Ca}^{2+}, \text{Mg}^{2+}$) but does NOT demineralize water ($\text{Na}^+$ salts remain in solution); ion-exchange resins remove ALL ions.
$\text{COD}$ is ALWAYS $\ge \text{BOD}$ because dichromate oxidizes both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organics.

conceptPrimer.heading: Why Hard Water Fails to Lather
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ wreck soap by precipitating insoluble stearates: $2\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{35}\text{COONa} + \text{Ca}^{2+} \to (\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{35}\text{COO})_2\text{Ca}\downarrow$ — the grey scum in a hard-water bucket IS calcium stearate. Micro-check: one $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ kills TWO soap molecules — that's why even moderate hardness wastes soap fast.

conceptPrimer.heading: Temporary vs Permanent: the Salt List Decides
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: TEMPORARY (carbonate) hardness comes from dissolved bicarbonates $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$ and $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$ — removable by mere boiling or Clark's lime. PERMANENT (non-carbonate) hardness comes from chlorides and sulphates $\text{CaCl}_2, \text{MgCl}_2, \text{CaSO}_4, \text{MgSO}_4$ — boiling does nothing; you need zeolite, Calgon or ion-exchange. Micro-check: any $\text{HCO}_3^-$ salt $=$ temporary; $\text{Cl}^-/\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ salts $=$ permanent.

conceptPrimer.heading: ppm: Everything Becomes CaCO₃ Equivalent
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Hardness is reported in ppm ($\text{mg/L}$) of $\text{CaCO}_3$ equivalent because $M(\text{CaCO}_3) = 100\ \text{g/mol}$ makes mental arithmetic clean. Each salt contributes $W \times \frac{100}{M}$; add the contributions. Units: $1\ \text{ppm} = 1\ \text{mg/L} = 0.1^\circ\text{Fr} = 0.07^\circ\text{Cl}$. Micro-check: $13.6\ \text{mg/L}$ $\text{CaSO}_4$ ($M = 136$): $13.6 \times \frac{100}{136} = 10\ \text{ppm}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Softening: Boiling, Clark's, Zeolite, Calgon, Resins
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Boiling/Clark's lime remove ONLY temporary hardness: $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaCO}_3\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$, but $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$ precipitates as $\text{Mg(OH)}_2\downarrow$ ($\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is less soluble than $\text{MgCO}_3$). For BOTH kinds: zeolite/permutit ($\text{Na}_2\text{Ze}$ exchanges $\text{Na}^+$; regenerated by $10\%\ \text{NaCl}$ brine), Calgon $\text{Na}_6\text{P}_6\text{O}_{18}$ (sequesters $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ as soluble $[\text{Na}_2\text{CaP}_6\text{O}_{18}]^{2-}$), and ion-exchange resins ($\text{R-H}^+ + \text{R'-OH}^-$) which DEMINERALIZE — removing all ions. Micro-check: zeolite softens but leaves $\text{Na}^+$ salts behind; only resins give deionized water.

conceptPrimer.heading: EDTA Complexometric Titration
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Quantitative hardness: titrate with disodium EDTA at $\text{pH} \approx 10$ ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ buffer) with Eriochrome Black-T indicator. $\text{Ca}^{2+}/\text{Mg}^{2+}$ first pull EBT into a wine-red complex; at the endpoint EDTA's stabler $1{:}1$ chelates steal the metal and free EBT shows pure blue. Micro-check: wine-red $\to$ blue means EDTA has won every $\text{M}^{2+}$ — that's the endpoint, at pH 10, never neutral.

conceptPrimer.heading: Potable Water and Pollution Metrics
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Disinfection: chlorination works through $\text{HOCl}$ (the real germicide, from $\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{HOCl} + \text{HCl}$), bleaching powder $\text{CaOCl}_2$, or ozone. Organic pollution: $\text{BOD}_5$ = dissolved $\text{O}_2$ consumed by microbes in 5 days at $20^\circ\text{C}$; COD = hot acidic $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ oxidation of ALL organics. Dichromate attacks biodegradable AND non-biodegradable matter, so $\text{COD} \ge \text{BOD}$ always. Micro-check: a sample whose COD far exceeds its BOD is loaded with non-biodegradable (industrial) organics.

keyDefinitions.definition: Water that fails to lather with soap due to dissolved $\text{Ca}^{2+}$/$\text{Mg}^{2+}$ salts.
Hardness from bicarbonates of Ca/Mg; removed by boiling or Clark's lime.
Hardness from chlorides/sulphates of Ca/Mg; needs zeolite, Calgon or resins.
$1\ \text{mg}$ CaCO₃ per litre — the universal hardness unit.
Hydrated sodium aluminosilicate $\text{Na}_2\text{Ze}$ exchanging $\text{Na}^+$ for $\text{Ca}^{2+}/\text{Mg}^{2+}$; regenerated with brine.
Sodium hexametaphosphate $\text{Na}_6\text{P}_6\text{O}_{18}$; sequesters hardness ions into soluble complexes.
Water freed of ALL dissolved ions by mixed cation ($\text{R-H}^+$) + anion ($\text{R'-OH}^-$) exchangers.
Hexadentate chelating agent giving $1{:}1$ complexes with $\text{Ca}^{2+}/\text{Mg}^{2+}$; basis of the hardness titration.
Biochemical Oxygen Demand: $\text{O}_2$ consumed in 5 days at $20^\circ\text{C}$ — biodegradable organic load.
Chemical Oxygen Demand: hot acidic dichromate oxidation of all organics; always $\ge$ BOD.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Which salt causes PERMANENT hardness of water?
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Chlorides and sulphates ($\text{MgCl}_2$) are permanent; bicarbonates are temporary; $\text{CaCO}_3$ is barely soluble and not the listed cause.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: A water sample contains $16.2\ \text{mg/L}$ of $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$ ($M = 162$). Its hardness contribution in ppm $\text{CaCO}_3$ is:

mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ has lower solubility ($K_{sp}$) than $\text{MgCO}_3$, so the hydroxide drops out — the classic trap; calcium bicarbonate gives $\text{CaCO}_3$.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: A spent zeolite (permutit) bed is regenerated using:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Brine floods the bed with $\text{Na}^+$, pushing $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ back off: $\text{CaZe} + 2\text{NaCl} \to \text{Na}_2\text{Ze} + \text{CaCl}_2$.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Calgon, the sequestering water softener, has the formula:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Calgon = sodium hexametaphosphate $\text{Na}_6\text{P}_6\text{O}_{18}$, binding $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ as soluble $[\text{Na}_2\text{CaP}_6\text{O}_{18}]^{2-}$.
Only paired $\text{R-H}^+$/$\text{R'-OH}^-$ resins strip ALL cations and anions; zeolite merely swaps $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ for $\text{Na}^+$.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The EDTA complexometric titration for hardness is carried out at:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: pH $\approx 10$, buffered with $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ — that's where EBT shows its endpoint colour change.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: In the EDTA titration with Eriochrome Black-T, the colour at the ENDPOINT is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Wine-red $[\text{Mg-EBT}]$ turns pure blue when EDTA has complexed all $\text{Ca}^{2+}/\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and released free EBT.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The correct relation between COD and BOD of a sample is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Dichromate oxidizes biodegradable AND non-biodegradable organics; microbes only handle the biodegradable — so COD is always the larger.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The active germicide produced when chlorine dissolves in water is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{HOCl} + \text{HCl}$: hypochlorous acid is the oxidizing germicide; $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{HCl}$ are inert bystanders.

memoryHooks: Scum is calcium stearate — hardness in one equation.
Bicarbonates boil away; chlorides and sulphates stay.
Zeolite swaps $\text{Na}^+$; brine brings the $\text{Na}^+$ back.
Calgon CAGES $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ — no precipitate, just a soluble complex.
Only mixed-bed resins make truly deionized water.
pH 10, EBT, wine-red to blue — the hardness titration trio.
COD $\ge$ BOD, always — dichromate eats what microbes can't.
commonMistakes: Using boiling or Clark's lime against permanent hardness.
Writing $\text{MgCO}_3$ as the boiling product of $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$ (it's $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$).
Claiming the zeolite process demineralizes water ($\text{Na}^+$ salts remain).
Multiplying by $M/100$ instead of $100/M$ in ppm conversion.
Running the EDTA titration at neutral pH or with the wrong buffer.
Attributing chlorination's kill to $\text{Cl}_2$ or $\text{Cl}^-$ instead of $\text{HOCl}$.
examChecklist: Classify every salt temporary vs permanent BEFORE converting.
ppm per salt: $W \times 100/M$; then ADD the contributions.
Boiling/Clark's = temporary only — say so explicitly.
EDTA trio: pH 10, $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ buffer, EBT red→blue.
$\text{HOCl}$ is the germicide; bleaching powder is $\text{CaOCl}_2$.
Close any BOD/COD question with COD $\ge$ BOD.
